speaker: ambrose_kettleby
text: Master Shakespeare? Ambrose Kettleby. From Somerset House, where I am sent up for my lord's linen and his letters.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Master Kettleby. How does my lord in Surrey?

speaker: ambrose_kettleby
text: Sound enough to ask after his players. He has heard the house is open and would know two things: that it opened quietly, and when the new king is to be seen.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: It opened quietly, sir. The new king is Thursday the second of October, if you will have a day.

speaker: ambrose_kettleby
text: My lord has a mind to see it, and says he will come unlooked-for. So I am to tell you he is coming.

speaker: ambrose_kettleby
text: Thursday the second of October. I have it down. Now, a small comfit from the court. My Lord Treasurer lies there very ill of the gout, and cannot stir hand nor foot, nor feed himself.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: What does that mean for players?

speaker: ambrose_kettleby
text: It means that every paper in England which wants his hand is waiting on his foot. Petitions. Warrants. Complaints out of the City.

speaker: ambrose_kettleby
text: My lord bids me say (and I soften it) that the City is never so busy with its pen as when the harvest is bad. You will keep an orderly house.

speaker: ambrose_kettleby
text: That is the county I should be anxious for. God keep you.
